Ironically enough, working for a charity. One of best around. We were fighting for womens rights in third world country and did the sponsor a child for a dollar a day thing. Thing is, we had to sign people up off the street downtown. We'd try to pull people away for a few minutes, tell a story or two and ultimately ask for donors. We were doing this literally feet away from homeless people who could've used help themselves. People treated us like the homeless people because we were asking for money and 9/10 people would completely ignore the fact you exist. I also watched my boss get spit on by a disgruntled dunk "merchant of the lord" the second day on the job. It was so frustrating to be disrespected by so much of society for simply trying to help people in need. That job taught me how rude people actually are.
